main_statement.latex: For every $\eps>0$, two $n\times n$ complex matrices can be multiplied using $O_\eps(n^{9/4+\eps})$ arithmetic operations. In particular, $\omega\leq9/4$.
main_statement.paraphrase: Over C, the matrix multiplication exponent is at most 2.25 (previous published record 2.371177, Dupont et al. 2026; the family's own M2 gives 2.258).

companion_statements.paraphrase: Over C: omega < 1129/500 = 2.258, alpha > 0.465, omega(1,0.709,1) < 2.092; transfer to char 0 and all but finitely many (uncomputed) primes.
Over every fixed field F (any characteristic): omega_F < 2.371054886006746.

lean_comparator.definitions_unfolded: Straight-line programs with constant/input/add/sub/mul gates (cost 1 per add/sub/mul, constants free, no division); MatrixAlgorithm F a b c correct iff eval = A*B for all A,B; AdmissibleExponent F tau := for all eps>0 exists C>0 for all n>=1 exists correct P with cost <= C n^(tau+eps); omega F := sInf {tau | AdmissibleExponent F tau}; rectangularOmega uses inner size ceil(n^k); complexAlpha := sSup {k in [0,1] | rectangularOmega C k = 2}.
lean_comparator.match_check: Matches the paper's arithmetic-operation model (M1 lines 39-43; M2 intro lines 9-21; M3 lines 3-6). Real.sInf/sSup junk values: sInf of an empty or unbounded-below set is 0, which would make '<= 9/4' vacuous; but the admissible set is nonempty (naive algorithm) and bounded below (every correct program for n>=1 has cost >=1, so tau >= 0), so the comparator is faithful. The alpha target requires rectangularOmega C k = 2 exactly, i.e. Lean must also prove the lower bound >= 2 (Arithmetic/LowerBound.lean exists). Note the comparator states <= 9/4 (non-strict), exactly as the paper.

barrier_analysis.AFLG_2015: Ambainis-Filmus-Le Gall: laser-method variants on CW powers (zeroing-out extraction) cannot beat ~2.3078. M2 evades it because extraction is a degeneration of T^{(x)n} (x) A_G with an auxiliary group tensor whose rank is charged and cancelled by multiplicity - outside the zeroing-out framework. M1 does not use CW tensors at all.
barrier_analysis.Alman_universal_method_and_CVZ_irreversi: Universal-method/irreversibility limit for CW_q is 2.16805 (Alman, ToC 2021; snippet). My own estimate for CW_1: R~=3, Q~=exp(1.0135)=2.755 (Strassen: tight tensors' asymptotic subrank = min of support functionals), irreversibility 1.084, barrier 2*1.084=2.168. So 2.290 and 2.258 from CW_1 are consistent with the barrier.
barrier_analysis.M1_route: M1 uses polynomial multiplication tensors C(a,a): R~=2a-1 and (estimate) Q~=a, so irreversibility log(2a-1)/log a -> 1 and the CVZ barrier tends to 2. M1 is moreover a dual (spectral) argument and never fixes one intermediate tensor. No known barrier excludes 9/4 by this route. These barrier numbers are my calculations from definitions, not quoted from the barrier papers.
barrier_analysis.Cohn_Umans: M2 notes the link to the group-theoretic approach; the Blasiak et al. 2017 limitation (bounded-exponent abelian groups cannot give omega=2) concerns embeddings of MM into group algebras, not this use of group tensors as separators; not binding.
